clue.text: Occasional pharmacist finally accomplished chemist's work

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word next to it

blocks.note: periodic means happening at intervals, now and then
the last letter of pharmacist
able means skilled or accomplished

explanation.surface: A pharmacist who only works occasionally has at last done something worthy of a chemist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chemist's work' suggests a pharmacy, but the chemist here is the scientist, and the work is Mendeleev's chart.
explanation.definitionFit: The periodic table is the chart of elements produced by a chemist, Dmitri Mendeleev, and is the core reference of chemistry.

clue.text: Earl with girl on his shoulder, a sign of his rank

definitions.text: on his shoulder, a sign of his rank

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for earl
Paulette is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An aristocrat with a girlfriend leaning on his shoulder, as a status symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a girl on the earl's shoulder; the whole closing phrase describes the shoulder ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is the ornamental shoulder piece on a uniform, often showing the wearer's military rank.

clue.text: Religious images prisoner found in Isiah

explanation.surface: A prisoner reads of sacred images in the Bible's book of Isaiah.
explanation.walkthrough: Isiah, as printed, is a slip for Isaiah, the Old Testament prophet, whose book is abbreviated Is.
explanation.definitionFit: Icons are painted images of holy figures venerated in Orthodox churches, so they are religious images.

clue.text: Left role during Act

blocks.note: an actor's role is their part
an act is a deed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' and 'role' suggest theatre, but the act is simply a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed is the past tense of depart, meaning went away, which matches left as a verb.

clue.text: Popular breakfast show in instalments on the radio

explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular breakfast show' reads as one radio programme; breakfast belongs to the definition and show to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal, such as cornflakes, is a common morning meal, so it is a popular breakfast.

clue.text: A chap entertains another by initially ordering a hot drink

blocks.note: taken as written
a chap is a man
another chap: Eric is a man's name
the first letter of ordering

explanation.surface: One man treats another to a hot drink, ordering it first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another chap, so it needs a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An americano is espresso diluted with hot water, a hot coffee drink.

clue.text: Without base shed inclined

indicators.note: in a down entry the base is the bottom letter, and without it that letter goes

blocks.note: a lean-to is a shed built against a wall

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a verb, as in cast off, but it is the garden building.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is the past tense of lean, meaning sloped or inclined to one side.

clue.text: Old show cruelly imitating ghastly politicians and egotistical stars primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each word gives its opening letter
cruelly suggests something treated roughly and twisted out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written into the mix
first letters of ghastly, politicians, egotistical and stars

explanation.surface: A description of a satirical TV programme that mocked politicians and celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: Spitting Image was a British TV satire (1984 to 1996) in which latex puppets lampooned politicians and stars, so the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting Image is a former British television show, so it fits old show.

clue.text: Something upon which you can vote

definitions.text: Something upon which you can vote

blocks.clueFragment: Something upon which you can vote
blocks.note: surface reading: a motion or proposal put to a ballot

blocks.clueFragment: Something upon which you can vote
blocks.note: setter's reading: a list you must be on to be allowed to vote at all

explanation.walkthrough: 'Vote upon' usually means decide a question; here 'upon' is literal, the register a voter's name has to be on.
explanation.definitionFit: The register of people entitled to vote in an area; being listed on it is what lets you vote.

clue.text: After gym start to overexert in a cool fog

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
in tells us one piece sits inside the following words

blocks.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
taken as written
cool and super are both slang for excellent
the first letter of overexert

explanation.surface: Someone back from the gym is warned not to overdo things in cold, foggy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' looks like temperature, matching the fog, but it is slang for great; 'in' tells you the first letter of overexert sits inside a cool word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is an old name for a thick, yellowish London smog, likened to pea soup.

clue.text: Messages your compiler rejected are sick

clue.text: Rings dipso about drinking litre after litre

clue.text: Hard-headed about boxer's movement lacking control

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer's movement' reads like the Ali shuffle, but it splits: the boxer's name with an S, then a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-headed means practical and unsentimental, which is what a realistic person is.

clue.text: One knight cared for fiancée

to tend is to look after

explanation.surface: A chivalrous knight once looked after his bride-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's intended is the one they are engaged to marry, so it is an old-fashioned word for a fiancée.

clue.text: Exotic entrance with one type of tree

blocks.note: taken as written into the mix

clue.text: Old vehicle initially left in a part of America?

the first letter of left
